Action.description:
The next step a person or the queue takes. A client that meets `unknown`
(a value from a newer engine) offers no action rather than guessing.

oneOf.description: Try again; the engine may already be doing so automatically.
Correct the submitted input.
Paste a refreshed link; private query values were not kept.
Send the download from the browser again.
Pick another destination.
Explicitly replace the existing file. Only a person may choose this.
Check the expected SHA-256 that was supplied.
Set up or repair the media helpers.
Inspect the media page again for a fresh set of choices.
The source's session expired; refresh the source and inspect it again.
The selected format vanished; create a linked replacement job.
Refresh the sign-in or other authorization.
Free disk space.
Lower concurrency or change policy.
Restart the engine or update Fetchpath so versions agree.
Fetch a fresh snapshot and try again.
Wait; the engine will continue on its own.

Wait for the person to approve or deny the job in Fetchpath. An
agent relays this rather than retrying.

AgentPolicy.description: What the person allows one agent to do without asking.

folders.description:
Folders the agent may save into, as full paths. A destination counts
as inside one only after links and junctions are resolved.

max_bytes.description: Largest download, in bytes, before it stops and waits for approval.

max_new_jobs_per_hour.description: New downloads per hour before further ones wait for approval.

ApprovalReason.description: Why a job waits for the person.

oneOf.description: The destination is not inside a folder granted to the agent.
The download passed the agent's size limit and stopped.
The agent asked for more new downloads per hour than it may.

ApprovalRequest.description: A job's wait for approval, as clients see it.

Command.description:
The command set. Names are the contract's where it has one, plus the
engine-level queries and controls from the platform design §4. Rules
arrive with FP-064; an engine that does not know a command answers
`contract.unknown_command`. Which principal may send which command is the
engine's decision (contract D1).

oneOf.description:
Several jobs at once, all or none: if any request is refused, none is
created. File jobs only, from the person.

retain_partial.description: Keep the partial file instead of removing staging bytes.

expected_sha256.description:
Replaces the expected SHA-256 before retrying; an empty string
removes it. The person only. Identity replacement revokes earlier
work (contract D2).

destination.description:
A new full path to save to, changed in the same step. The person
only; an agent uses `ResolveDestination`.

oneOf.description:
Removes a finished or failed job from the list. Its history entry and
ledger records follow the retention rules.

query.description: Matched against display links and file names.

oneOf.description:
Media pages the person sent from the browser, to be opened for a
format choice. Each is returned once. The person only.

Lets a job that is `awaiting_approval` run. Approving a size stop
lifts the limit for that job only.
Refuses a job that is `awaiting_approval`; it ends `cancelled`.

Sets one agent's access, or removes it with `null`, so the agent is
back to asking for everything.

Replays durable events after `after_seq`, or answers with a snapshot
boundary when they were compacted, then streams new ones.
The same for every job, ordered by the engine-wide `cursor`.

CommandEnvelope.description:
Every command a client sends. The engine deduplicates by
`(client_id, command_id)` and acknowledges only after the mutation commits,
so a client that lost the reply resends the same envelope unchanged.

expected_revision.description:
The job revision the client last saw. A mismatch returns
`contract.revision_conflict` without changing anything.

CommandResult.description:
A successful command's result. A repeated command returns its original
result even if the job has moved on since (contract §5).

oneOf.description: One job, after the command.

`Pause` and `Cancel`: whether the request was taken, per the contract's
command/state matrix. `accepted` means intent is recorded; the
outcome arrives later as a state event.
`TakeLinkReviews`: links as the browser sent them, never shown whole.

The subscription starts here: every retained event after `position`
follows, then new ones.

The requested events were compacted. These snapshots are atomic with
the stream, which continues after `position`.
Every agent the person configured, sorted by name.
The engine is stopping after finishing in-flight work safely.

ConflictPolicy.description: What happens when the destination already exists.

oneOf.description: Stop and wait for a decision. Nothing is overwritten.
Replace the existing file. Requires explicit intent from a person.
Already in the requested state.
The job already finished or was cancelled.
Pause after the publication fence.
Cancel after the publication fence.
A cancellation is already under way with its own cleanup policy.

DestinationDecision.description: The answer to a destination conflict.

path.description: A full local path including the file name.

EngineSettings.description:
Engine settings. The engine clamps every value into range and reports
what it applied.

start_engine_at_sign_in.description:
Start the engine when the person signs in to Windows, so schedules
survive a restart. Off unless the person turns it on. Absent from an
update means "leave it as it is", so a client that does not know the
setting cannot turn it off by accident.

oneOf.description: One frame or connection; other connections are unaffected.
One command; nothing was changed.
One job's recorded failure.
The engine as a whole.

IntegrityOutcome.description: What a finished download's bytes are known to be (contract §3).

oneOf.description: Matches a trusted expected hash.

Consistent with a strong source validator; the publisher was not
independently checked.
A hash was recorded but there was nothing trusted to compare it with.
Did not match the required hash; never published as a success.

JobEvent.description:
A durable job event. `seq` rises by exactly one per job; `cursor` orders
events across all jobs. Delivery may repeat, so clients deduplicate by
`(job_id, seq)`.

oneOf.description:
An event kind this client does not know, from a newer engine. Its
`seq` still counts, so the stream has no gap.
Not yet completed or cancelled.
Waiting for the person to approve or deny.

JobInput.description: Where a job's bytes come from.

oneOf.description:
A request already held by the engine, such as a browser capture. The
secret stays where it is stored.

JobRequest.description:
The immutable request a job is created from (contract §4). Changing any
of it later creates a new job.

expected_sha256.description:
A SHA-256 as the person supplied it. Nothing that does not match
it is published.

variant_id.description: The variant id from a media inspection.

JobSnapshot.description:
One job as a client sees it. Every snapshot carries the revision and the
last durable event sequence it reflects, so a client can resume its event
stream exactly after it.

cleanup_pending.description: Staging bytes are still waiting to be removed.

destination.description: The local file path. An agent sees only jobs it created (contract D1).

expected_sha256.description: The SHA-256 the person supplied, lowercase hex.

not_before.description: Do not start before this instant.

observed_sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the bytes received. Records what arrived; it is not
evidence of what the publisher intended.

retry_at.description: When an automatic retry is due.

source_display.description: The link without user info, query or fragment.

JobState.description:
The contract's job states (§6). A scheduled job is `queued` with a
`not_before`, not a separate state.

oneOf.description:
Asked for by an agent outside its policy; waits for the person to
approve or deny it (contract D1).
A state this client does not know, from a newer engine.

MediaInspection.description:
What a media page offers. `title` comes from the page and is untrusted
text.

MediaVariant.description:
One format a media page offers. Sizes are the helper's estimates until it
resolves them.

PolicyPatch.description: Mutable policy. Absent fields are left as they are.

Principal.description: Who a connection acts for: user, browser or agent:<name>.

Progress.description:
Progress facts (contract §7). An unknown total is `null`, never zero, and
there is no remaining time without both a total and a rate.

ProgressSample.description:
An ephemeral progress sample. It never consumes `seq` and may be dropped
or coalesced for a slow client; the current aggregate is in every
snapshot.

ProtocolError.description:
A protocol error. Diagnostics are redacted before they reach this type:
no cookies, authorization headers, signed query strings or private paths.

retry_after_seconds.description: A bounded wait before retrying, when the error is retryable.

QueueStats.description: Queue figures counted from one reconciled moment.

combined_bytes_per_second.description: Sum of observed per-download rates, not a link-capacity measurement.

Reply.description:
The answer to one command. `command_id` is absent only when the command
could not be read far enough to find it.

oneOf.description: Start as soon as a slot is free.

Segment.description: One byte range in flight: received into memory, not yet written.

SensitiveUrl.description: A link as given, possibly with secrets in it. Never displayed or logged as is.

ServerMessage.description: Every frame from the engine to a client.

SettingsView.description: Settings as stored plus the limits the engine enforces.

repaired.description: The stored file was unusable and defaults were substituted.

WaitingReason.description: Why a non-terminal job is waiting.

oneOf.description: A private link's query was not kept, so a refreshed link is needed.
A browser capture's protected context is gone.
Something already exists at the destination.
A media format must be chosen.
The media helpers are missing.

description: Every frame is one message: a CommandEnvelope from a client, or a ServerMessage from the engine.
